constraints: Presence is optional and may expire independently of the reply.
A sent reply can fail even while the agent remains online.

feedback.reason: Presence is transient, but reply delivery is durable; expose each with its own labeled state.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A non-color cue identifies presence, while the sent/failed reply state persists independently of that cue.
details.scenarioApplication: A support agent claims a conversation while a presence indicator changes independently of the durable reply. How should the UI communicate presence and reply state to someone who cannot distinguish color cues?
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If presence expires while delivery is pending, keep the delivery result available until the agent resolves it.
details.errorCorrection: Hue alone does not expose which state changed to a user who cannot distinguish the colors.
details.transfer: If the agent’s reply fails after presence expires, retain the failed reply state even though the online indicator disappears.

messages.text: Hue alone does not expose which state changed to a user who cannot distinguish the colors.
Replacing one status value when presence changes can erase the independent sent or failed reply result.
Choose a labeled cue for presence; the two states have different lifetimes and are not interchangeable.
A brief flash can disappear before the agent confirms whether the reply was delivered.
Being online does not confirm that the reply reached the server.
Choose a labeled cue for durable reply delivery; the two states have different lifetimes and are not interchangeable.

values.text: Keep presence and reply labels separate, but use a color change as the only online cue.
Label presence with text or shape; keep the durable reply result in its own state.
Use one labeled value, Online or Reply sent, and replace it whenever presence changes.
Keep pending, sent, or failed text beside the reply and retain it after the agent leaves.
Show the delivery result in a toast; keep it available while the conversation remains open.
Show a labeled online state and a temporary send notice, then infer delivery from continued presence.

prompt: A support agent claims a conversation while a presence indicator changes independently of the durable reply. How should the UI communicate presence and reply state to someone who cannot distinguish color cues?

constraints: The article title and search actions must remain in the same usable task at 200% text zoom.
Loading and selection states must not depend on hue alone.

feedback.reason: Enlarged content is useful only if the article and its actions stay reachable.

details.mechanismOrProperty: At 200% text zoom, the article may wrap vertically; a fixed canvas or delayed status can separate an action from the content or hide whether a result is active.
details.scenarioApplication: In a public content site, the reader must open a localized article from search. At 200% zoom, the localized article title and search actions must reflow without disappearing. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable? The article title and search actions must remain in the same usable task at 200% text zoom. Loading and selection states must not depend on hue alone.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Text enlargement at 200% is not the 320 CSS-pixel reflow test; the localized article and its actions must remain usable without horizontal scrolling.
details.errorCorrection: The side rail keeps controls tied to the desktop canvas; at 200% text zoom it can force two-dimensional navigation for ordinary content.
details.transfer: If forced colors remove the result highlight, keep the selected result and loading status identifiable without color.

messages.text: The side rail keeps controls tied to the desktop canvas; at 200% text zoom it can force two-dimensional navigation for ordinary content.
A delayed status leaves loading and selection ambiguous while the user is acting; provide a concurrent non-color cue.
Uniform scaling preserves the desktop composition instead of allowing the article and actions to reflow independently.

options.text: Keep a readable article width and move the search actions into a fixed side rail that may require horizontal scrolling at 200%.
Use color for result loading and selection, with a short textual status announced only after the search finishes.
Let the article and actions wrap at 200%; show loading and selection with persistent text or shape as well as color.
Scale the full desktop canvas uniformly so article and actions keep their original relative positions.

prompt: In a public content site, the reader must open a localized article from search. At 200% zoom, the localized article title and search actions must reflow without disappearing. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?

constraints: the dashboard has a bounded freshness budget and a slow network
The live vehicle position should remain understandable with reduced motion and a static selected-vehicle state.

feedback.reason: Dispatch still needs vehicle identity and freshness when movement is reduced.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Animation is a presentation of changing coordinates, not the state itself. A static marker, selected-vehicle label, and update age communicate the same decision without requiring tracking.
details.scenarioApplication: In a fleet dashboard, the fleet manager must monitor vehicles and drill into one vehicle. The live vehicle position should remain understandable with reduced motion and a static selected-vehicle state. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Reduced motion changes how position is presented, not the dispatcher’s need for current coordinates or an explicit stale-data age.
details.errorCorrection: Continuous motion still creates the tracking demand that the preference is meant to reduce; add a stable equivalent.
details.transfer: If the position feed pauses, preserve its last-known marker and age instead of implying that a static marker is current.

messages.text: Continuous motion still creates the tracking demand that the preference is meant to reduce; add a stable equivalent.
Reduced motion changes presentation, not the need to identify and inspect a vehicle; keep the task information available.
Hue and hover do not provide a persistent, perceivable selection and freshness cue across input modes.

options.text: Keep the moving marker because its animation communicates position more precisely than a static label.
Stop all position updates and hide the selected vehicle when the user requests reduced motion.
Use marker hue for selection and freshness, with a tooltip available on hover for the latest timestamp.
Keep a static selected-position cue and freshness time when motion is reduced; retain the vehicle label.

prompt: In a fleet dashboard, the fleet manager must monitor vehicles and drill into one vehicle. The live vehicle position should remain understandable with reduced motion and a static selected-vehicle state. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?

constraints: media playback, markers, and upload processing fail independently
At 200% zoom, playback markers and upload controls must remain visible, with a static status equivalent.

feedback.reason: A saved marker and a transferred recording are different outcomes.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The timeline can confirm marker persistence independently from upload. Reflow keeps marker controls in view, while persistent text substitutes for movement as the save confirmation.
details.scenarioApplication: In an audio production studio, the producer must preview a recording and save markers. At 200% zoom, playback markers and upload controls must remain visible, with a static status equivalent. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Marker persistence, playback, and upload progress are independent; a saved marker must not be mistaken for an uploaded recording.
details.errorCorrection: A transient pulse can end before the producer confirms a marker was saved; the state needs a persistent equivalent.
details.transfer: If the upload fails while playback continues, keep marker-saved and transfer-failed states separate and persistent.

messages.text: A transient pulse can end before the producer confirms a marker was saved; the state needs a persistent equivalent.
A motion preference should not remove the audio editing task; playback and marker operations can remain available with calmer feedback.
At zoom, overflow can move marker controls outside the visible task area; the panel needs to reflow.

options.text: Let markers and upload controls reflow; confirm a saved marker with a persistent state when motion is reduced.
Show a brief waveform pulse when a marker is saved, then return to the unchanged timeline.
Disable playback and marker editing together whenever reduced motion is enabled.
Keep the timeline at its desktop width and let marker controls overflow rather than moving them below it.

prompt: In an audio production studio, the producer must preview a recording and save markers. At 200% zoom, playback markers and upload controls must remain visible, with a static status equivalent. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?

constraints: The draft cannot become reader-visible until publishing succeeds.
The preview and publish action must remain available at 200% text zoom.

feedback.reason: A preview remains a draft until an authorized publish succeeds; zoom must not hide that distinction.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Keep a visible draft label and let preview controls wrap so Publish stays available at 200%.
details.scenarioApplication: An editor previews a draft while the published article remains available to readers. At 200% zoom, how should the preview label and publish action remain distinguishable?
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A draft label communicates state but does not itself grant publication authority; report the server’s publish result.
details.errorCorrection: A color change alone does not identify the publication state.
details.transfer: If the editor zooms while the publish request is pending, preserve the draft state and reachable action until the server confirms the transition.

messages.text: A color change alone does not identify the publication state.
Visual similarity between copies does not identify which one is published.
This dimension must preserve draft-versus-published authority.
Clipping the toolbar hides an action required to publish.
Shrinking text and targets undermines zoom and can make the action difficult to operate.
This dimension must preserve a reachable publish action at 200% zoom.

values.text: Label draft and published copies, but distinguish their state only with a badge color.
Label the preview Draft and reuse that label on the reader-facing copy after publication.
Keep the preview labeled Draft and identify the published copy with its own textual state.
Keep the toolbar on one row; scroll it horizontally to reach Publish at 200% zoom.
Wrap the toolbar controls so the draft state and Publish action remain visible at 200%.
Keep all toolbar actions visible at 200% by reducing type size and hit-area dimensions.

prompt: An editor previews a draft while the published article remains available to readers. At 200% zoom, how should the preview label and publish action remain distinguishable?

constraints: the upload can pause and resume without corrupting the final asset
At 200% zoom and with reduced motion, upload progress plus Pause and Resume must remain available.

feedback.reason: The upload must remain controllable and its terminal state must be knowable.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Pause and resume are task actions; pending, paused, failed, and complete are distinct states. Text or shape keeps those distinctions when motion or color is unavailable.
details.scenarioApplication: In a media library, the curator must upload a large video and inspect its processing state. At 200% zoom and with reduced motion, upload progress plus Pause and Resume must remain available. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The progress label must survive pauses, failures, retries, and completion; animation cannot be the only evidence of transfer state.
details.errorCorrection: Hover-only actions are unavailable to touch and can disappear under zoom; pausing must remain an explicit reachable choice.
details.transfer: If the file pauses and the user enlarges text, keep Resume visible and distinguish paused from a completed transfer.

messages.text: Hover-only actions are unavailable to touch and can disappear under zoom; pausing must remain an explicit reachable choice.
The same label for active and complete states hides whether the asset is ready; color and animation alone are insufficient.
Abbreviating status can remove the distinctions needed to resume or recover; allow the row to wrap and controls to move.

options.text: Keep the upload running at zoom and reveal Pause or Resume only in a hover menu beside the progress bar.
Use an animated progress bar that changes hue at completion, while keeping the label fixed to “Uploading”.
Keep progress, Pause, and Resume reachable at 200%; label paused, failed, and complete states persistently.
Preserve a fixed-width progress row and abbreviate file and status labels when they exceed its width.

prompt: In a media library, the curator must upload a large video and inspect its processing state. At 200% zoom and with reduced motion, upload progress plus Pause and Resume must remain available. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?

constraints: the mutation must reconcile with server version and audit state
The reservation confirmation must distinguish pending, accepted, and rejected states without hue alone.

feedback.reason: Only the server response establishes whether the reservation was accepted.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Pending state must not be styled as success. A persistent row state remains available after a transient notification disappears.
details.scenarioApplication: In a booking administration panel, the operator must move a reservation and notify the guest. The reservation confirmation must distinguish pending, accepted, and rejected states without hue alone. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Pending is not accepted: only the authoritative server response determines the reservation outcome, which must outlast the toast.
details.errorCorrection: Optimistic feedback can imply success before the authoritative response; distinguish submitting from accepted.
details.transfer: If the operator leaves and returns after a rejected move, keep the rejection visible in the reservation row.

messages.text: Optimistic feedback can imply success before the authoritative response; distinguish submitting from accepted.
A transient toast can disappear before the operator returns to the reservation; keep its state in the row.
After motion ends, the same label loses the decision result; retain a textual or shape cue.

options.text: Mark the reservation accepted immediately on submit and replace that state if the server later rejects it.
Show the server result in a temporary toast, then return the reservation to an unmarked row.
Use a distinct transition animation for acceptance and rejection; the settled row can share one neutral label.
Show pending, accepted, and rejected as persistent text or shape cues; retain the server result after a toast closes.

prompt: In a booking administration panel, the operator must move a reservation and notify the guest. The reservation confirmation must distinguish pending, accepted, and rejected states without hue alone. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?

constraints: the client can guide input but cannot enforce protected pricing
The discount and order outcome must remain visually distinct without relying on color alone.

feedback.reason: Price eligibility and a placed order are separate claims.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The client can display a quote or discount, but only the server-authorized order result confirms the protected price; persistent text and shape preserve both steps.
details.scenarioApplication: In a retail checkout, the shopper must apply a discount and place an order. The discount and order outcome must remain visually distinct without relying on color alone. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A visible discount or order state does not enforce pricing; protected price authority remains server-side.
details.errorCorrection: A client-side eligibility cue cannot establish the server-authorized price; show pending and confirmed separately.
details.transfer: If the server rejects an eligible discount, show that eligibility did not mean the order price was accepted.

messages.text: A client-side eligibility cue cannot establish the server-authorized price; show pending and confirmed separately.
Low contrast can obscure the state rather than reduce clutter; preserve a visible distinction and sufficient contrast.
A badge is presentation, not price authority, and removing it hides the accepted order outcome.

options.text: Separate discount eligibility from server-confirmed order status with persistent, high-contrast cues.
Apply the displayed discount as accepted at submit and reconcile the order total only if the server rejects it.
Use the same low-contrast neutral treatment for discount, pending, and confirmed order to avoid visual emphasis.
Show a high-contrast green discount badge as the confirmation of the protected price, then remove it after checkout.

prompt: In a retail checkout, the shopper must apply a discount and place an order. The discount and order outcome must remain visually distinct without relying on color alone. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?

constraints: URL filters, current server results, and row selection have separate lifetimes.
At 200% text zoom, row actions and selection still need a usable viewport.

feedback.reason: At 200% zoom, ordinary controls must stay reachable; a table viewport may scroll in two dimensions if its row actions do not obscure data and selection is non-color.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A data table can retain its row-column relationships in a focused two-dimensional viewport; reflow its toolbar/actions where practical and expose selected rows with a checkbox or text as well as color.
details.scenarioApplication: An administrative table supports sorting, filtering, pagination, and export. At 200% zoom, which layout keeps row actions and the selected-row state available without relying on color alone?
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not force every data column into a narrow stack if that destroys row comparison; keep a clear viewport and its actions usable.
details.errorCorrection: Pinning actions over cell contents hides the very values being compared; fixed desktop columns can also push actions out of view. Keep the viewport usable and its row actions clear.
details.transfer: If forced colors remove row background styling, preserve selection with an explicit checkbox or selected-state label.

messages.text: Pinned actions that cover cell values obscure the data being compared; keep actions visible without overlaying row content.
Removing row actions at zoom prevents the requested task.
This dimension must preserve usable row actions and data access at zoom.
Color alone cannot communicate selected-row state to every user.
Hover does not persist as selected state and is unavailable to many inputs.
This dimension must preserve selected-row identification without color alone.

values.text: Reflow table actions or focus a usable table viewport that retains row relationships.
Keep a scrollable column viewport and pin row actions at its edge, even when they cover cell values.
Keep all columns visible at high zoom; move row actions into a menu outside the selected row.
Use a high-contrast selected-row background and keep the existing checkbox unchecked.
Keep a checkbox in each row, but show its checked state only while the pointer hovers.
Pair the selected-row color with a checked box or selected label in that row.

prompt: An administrative table supports sorting, filtering, pagination, and export. At 200% zoom, which layout keeps row actions and the selected-row state available without relying on color alone?

constraints: The query and refinements must reproduce the same view from a shared URL.
Cancellation is a distinct user intent and must remain visible while an obsolete request may still return.

feedback.reason: Serialize query and filters in the URL; show loading separately from cancellation and keep Cancel reachable.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The URL serializes buyer intent; a request identifier and explicit Cancel state describe work in flight. A late response must not replace the newer query.
details.scenarioApplication: A buyer searches and refines a marketplace view. The request can be canceled, and a shared URL must reproduce the query and filters. Which treatment keeps URL state and loading or cancellation state distinct? The query and refinements must reproduce the same view from a shared URL. Cancellation is a distinct user intent and must remain visible while an obsolete request may still return.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A reproducible URL captures query and refinement state, not a promise that its request succeeded; cancellation and the eventual result remain separate states.
details.errorCorrection: A spinner alone conflates an active request with a canceled one; local-only refinements also disappear when the link is opened elsewhere.
details.transfer: If the buyer changes a filter while the previous request is still returning, update the URL to the new view and ignore any response that no longer matches it.

messages.text: The shared URL is correct, but one spinner cannot distinguish an active request from a cancellation.
A cancellation label is insufficient if the shared URL omits refinements and restores a different buyer view.
The URL reproduces intent, but disabling Cancel removes the required way to supersede a pending request.

options.text: Keep query and filters in the URL, but use one spinner that disappears on either completion or cancellation.
Keep a visible cancel status, but store refinements only in local state so the URL opens a different view.
Serialize query and filters in the URL; show loading separately from cancellation and keep Cancel reachable.
Reproduce the view from the URL, but disable cancellation until the request finishes.

prompt: A buyer searches and refines a marketplace view. The request can be canceled, and a shared URL must reproduce the query and filters. Which treatment keeps URL state and loading or cancellation state distinct?

constraints: the active revision and comment anchors must remain attributable
The active revision and comment anchor must remain distinguishable at high zoom without color alone.

feedback.reason: An anchor must identify the commented text in the active revision even when layout reflows.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Store the comment against a stable paragraph or text range plus revision ID; zoom changes wrapping and screen position, not the anchor identity.
details.scenarioApplication: The author edits a paragraph while a reviewer comments. At high zoom, the active revision and the paragraph receiving each comment must remain identifiable without color alone.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A visual marker may move as text wraps, but the comment remains attached to the same content and revision; incoming comments must not silently retarget it.
details.errorCorrection: An animated marker shows movement rather than durable association, while a colored underline alone does not identify the revision or remain perceivable in forced colors.
details.transfer: If the paragraph is edited after the comment arrives, retain the revision and range association or explicitly show that the anchor needs resolution.

messages.text: Animation does not persist as an anchor after arrival and can distract during simultaneous edits; keep a stable marker.
The underline can disappear in forced colors and comment text does not establish which revision is active.
Fixed columns can make comment actions unreachable as text or zoom expands; allow the regions to reflow.

options.text: Animate the paragraph anchor toward each incoming comment so the reviewer can infer its destination.
Highlight the selected comment with a colored underline and rely on the comment text for revision identity.
Keep editor and comments in fixed columns, allowing horizontal overflow when translated paragraphs grow.
Keep revision and comment anchors identifiable with persistent cues; let the editor and controls reflow at zoom.

prompt: In a collaborative research editor, the author must edit a paragraph while another reviewer comments. The active revision and comment anchor must remain distinguishable at high zoom without color alone. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?

constraints: the signed evidence must identify the exact revision
The exact signed revision must remain identified without relying on a colored badge.

feedback.reason: Signature evidence is useful only when it names the exact content version that was signed.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Bind the signature record to an immutable revision identifier and keep that identifier beside the resulting evidence; wrapping preserves the association at zoom.
details.scenarioApplication: The signer must open and sign the current revision. The completed evidence needs to identify that precise version without relying on badge color.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A signature record proves an action on one version; a title, current page, or generic signed badge can refer to a different revision later.
details.errorCorrection: A persistent badge without the revision identifier cannot distinguish which version was signed; a secondary panel makes the evidence harder to verify at the action point.
details.transfer: If a new revision is published after signing, show the signed revision ID with the existing signature rather than relabeling it as current.

messages.text: A title transition does not identify the signed version, and hiding details behind another step weakens immediate verification.
A signature indicator without revision identity cannot show which document version was signed.
The exact revision is essential evidence; do not sacrifice it to preserve a fixed-width toolbar.

options.text: Keep the signed revision identifier beside persistent signature evidence, with both readable at zoom.
Animate the document title after signing and show the revision details only when the signer opens a secondary panel.
Show a persistent high-contrast signature badge but omit the revision identifier to keep the confirmation compact.
Keep the signature action in place by shrinking or clipping revision details when the signer zooms in.

prompt: In a document-signing workspace, the signer must open and sign the current document revision. The exact signed revision must remain identified without relying on a colored badge. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?

constraints: The camera can become unavailable independently from network transfer.
Pause, failure, and completion must be distinguishable during the large upload.

feedback.reason: Transfer progress must identify its current state, while controls stay reachable on the small capture screen.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Text labels distinguish pending, paused, failed, and completed transfer states; keeping Pause, Resume, and Retry outside an overlay preserves access to the file identity and status.
details.scenarioApplication: The technician captures evidence while camera capability or network availability may change. During a large upload on a small screen, they must tell which transfer state is active and reach its recovery controls.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Camera permission and network transfer are independent: a camera becoming unavailable does not prove that a captured file failed to upload. A progress indicator cannot promise server receipt before confirmation.
details.errorCorrection: A percentage with an unchanged Uploading label cannot distinguish paused from complete; a footer covering the upload status hides the file and its transfer state.
details.transfer: If camera permission is lost after capture, keep the selected file and its network transfer status available; report completion only after the transfer is confirmed.

messages.text: The percentage does not distinguish a paused transfer from a completed one while the label remains Uploading.
A success color and short label do not preserve separate pending, paused, failed, and completed states.
Choose a text state that distinguishes pause, failure, and confirmed completion beside progress.
A footer over the status can hide the file identity and progress on a small screen.
An animated retry cue depends on motion; keep retry visible and understandable without animation.
Keep transfer controls reachable without obscuring the active file and its state.

values.text: Label pending, paused, failed, and completed states beside the upload progress.
Show a percentage and retain the Uploading label until the server confirms completion.
Show progress text while active, then use a success color and a brief completion label.
Pin Pause, Resume, and Retry over the upload status on a small screen, obscuring the file and transfer state.
Keep Pause, Resume, and Retry reachable and reduce nonessential movement.
Keep the controls reachable, but animate the retry affordance only while the upload is paused.

prompt: A technician captures evidence when camera capability or network availability may change mid-task. Which progress treatment remains perceivable and operable while a large upload runs on a small screen?

constraints: long localized names and slow devices are expected
Validation errors and confirmation must stay readable when long names expand the form.

feedback.reason: A useful validation result names the failed field and leaves a readable route to correct and resubmit it.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Associate each error with its field and expose a direct correction path; allow long attendee names and messages to wrap instead of shrinking or clipping them.
details.scenarioApplication: The attendee registers with a long name, may need to correct a validation error, and needs a readable confirmation after submit as translated content expands.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A summary can supplement inline errors, but it must link or move focus to the relevant field. Confirmation remains a separate server result after correction.
details.errorCorrection: A red border alone does not explain the error, and a plain summary without field links makes the attendee search again through the expanded form.
details.transfer: If the attendee corrects one field but another remains invalid, preserve the entered values and direct them to the remaining field without truncating its label.

messages.text: A summary that cannot move focus to the invalid field adds a second navigation search, especially with long labels.
A border may not be perceived as an error and delaying the reason forces a repeated failure before correction.
Shortening names or labels can hide the field identity; allow the form to grow and labels to wrap.

options.text: Focus a summary of invalid fields after submit, but leave its entries as plain text without links to the fields.
Mark invalid fields with a strong red border and expose the reason only after the attendee submits again.
Let translated names and errors wrap; associate each error with its field and preserve contrast for correction.
Keep the form in a fixed-width grid and shorten translated labels and names to preserve the desktop row height.

prompt: In an event-registration site, the attendee must register, recover a validation error, and receive confirmation. Validation errors and confirmation must stay readable when long names expand the form. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?

constraints: assignment, exposure, rollback, and telemetry must be correlated
Experiment assignment, exposure, and rollback status must not be distinguished by color alone.

feedback.reason: Assignment, exposure, and rollback are separate experiment events and need independent persistent evidence.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Stable experiment and cohort identifiers correlate assignment and exposure records; an explicit rollback request remains pending until the server confirms its result.
details.scenarioApplication: The product engineer rolls out a client change to one cohort and must distinguish assignment, exposure, and rollback without depending on color.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A rollback request stopping or its indicator disappearing does not mean the server completed rollback; keep each state available until its authoritative result arrives.
details.errorCorrection: One cohort color cannot show which event occurred, and a transient pulse ending cannot establish whether rollback succeeded or failed.
details.transfer: If the server rejects rollback after exposure was recorded, retain both the exposure event and rejected rollback result against the same cohort ID.

messages.text: The same hue cannot identify which of three independent states changed; each row needs a direct state cue.
A stopped request may have failed rather than rolled back; keep the authoritative result visible after motion ends.
A remote legend forces users to map color and can fail in forced colors; label each state in context.

options.text: Use the same cohort color for assignment, exposure, and rollback, with the experiment name as the only textual label.
Pulse the rollback indicator while waiting for the server and remove it as soon as the request stops.
Use a consistent legend of three colors for the states, without labels in each cohort row.
Keep assignment, exposure, and rollback separately labeled; retain calm persistent states while results are pending.

prompt: In an experiment console, the product engineer must roll out a client change to one cohort. Experiment assignment, exposure, and rollback status must not be distinguished by color alone. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?

constraints: the map must remain usable on a low-end tablet
The selected route and live position must remain available with reduced motion and 200% zoom.

feedback.reason: Route selection, turn guidance, and position freshness answer different dispatch questions.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Keep the selected route and next turn as stable labeled data; show the last position with its age, and provide a static equivalent when reduced motion is requested.
details.scenarioApplication: The dispatcher adjusts a route while following a live position stream, and must still read the selected route and current position at 200% zoom with reduced motion.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A static position remains useful only with an update age; the motion preference changes presentation, not freshness or route authority. Reflow must keep the route summary and map actions separate.
details.errorCorrection: A moving marker does not identify the selected route or turn, and hiding the route label removes context exactly when motion is reduced.
details.transfer: If the feed becomes stale while the route changes, retain the chosen route and show the age of the last position rather than implying a live update.

messages.text: A moving position does not identify the selected route or turn; persistent labels support route decisions.
A motion preference must not remove route information needed for dispatch; retain a static cue.
Overlap can hide the next turn or selected route at zoom; the map summary and controls need room to reflow.

options.text: Keep route, next turn, and position age readable at zoom; offer a static position cue under reduced motion.
Keep the vehicle marker moving and infer the selected route from the map path and live animation.
Remove the route label when reduced motion is active while preserving the map and moving vehicle marker.
Keep turn controls in a fixed map toolbar and allow them to overlap the route summary at zoom.

prompt: In a logistics route planner, the dispatcher must adjust a route while a live position stream is visible. The selected route and live position must remain available with reduced motion and 200% zoom. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?

constraints: Filters must be shareable and separate from reorder submission.
Filter, reset, and reorder targets must meet WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 without relying on an exception, and selected filters need a non-color cue.

feedback.reason: Target separation reduces accidental activation; URL-backed filter state preserves the shared view without submitting a reorder.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Distinct pointer targets reduce slips between filter, reset, and reorder; URL-backed filter values serialize view state while reorder submission remains a separate action.
details.scenarioApplication: The manager shares a filtered inventory view and submits a reorder from touch. Each filter, reset, and reorder target must satisfy WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8; the selected filters must also be perceivable without color, and the shared URL must not submit the order.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: SC 2.5.8 requires a 24 CSS-pixel minimum unless a stated exception applies; 44 CSS pixels is the enhanced 2.5.5 target, not a blanket minimum. Here the 20-pixel targets have no spacing or other exception. A checkmark is a non-color cue, but this option provides none. URL-backed filters do not authorize or replay a reorder.
details.errorCorrection: Twenty-pixel adjacent targets fall below the AA minimum with no exception; separate spacing is relevant only when using the criterion’s spacing exception. A checkmark would supplement chip color, but this option explicitly omits both text and shape cues.
details.transfer: If the manager copies the filtered view before placing an order, reopening the link should restore the selected filters while leaving reorder unsubmitted.

messages.text: These 20 CSS-pixel targets have no spacing or other exception, so they miss SC 2.5.8’s 24-pixel minimum.
A precision swipe excludes users who cannot perform that gesture.
This dimension must preserve a usable pointer target without a blanket 44 CSS-pixel rule.
A checkmark is an alternative non-color cue, but this option explicitly omits text and shape cues, leaving chip state color-only.
A visible summary helps locally, but omitting filters from the URL makes a shared link restore a different view.
This dimension must preserve visible active filters separate from reset or submit.

values.text: Use adjacent 20 CSS-pixel filter, reset, and submit targets with no spacing or other target-size exception.
Separate filter and submit controls with suitable target size and spacing.
Make reorder a touch action and expose filters through a swipe gesture from the list edge.

feedback.reason: Local selection is intent; a remote board update is a separate actor’s state until the move is acknowledged.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A remote update must not erase the facilitator’s local intent or imply that the local move has committed.
details.errorCorrection: The same highlight conflates local intent with remote state; users need to tell which actor changed the card.
details.transfer: If a remote update changes the selected card’s column, show that change without erasing the facilitator’s pending move.

messages.text: The same highlight conflates local intent with remote state; users need to tell which actor changed the card.

constraints: The status panel must identify the selected file and distinguish uploading, complete, and failed states without echoing its protected fields.
At 200% zoom, the progress and recovery action must remain readable together.

feedback.reason: Minimal local file identity distinguishes this transfer; persistent text state and readable recovery controls preserve progress without exposing document contents.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A filename or safe case identifier disambiguates the active transfer; a text status distinguishes progress from completion or failure. Wrapping keeps Retry or Review reachable at text zoom without echoing document fields.
details.scenarioApplication: The case worker uploads a confidential file and must know which file is moving, whether it completed, and what to do after failure. The status panel must stay readable at 200% zoom while protected field values remain out of the display.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Show only metadata approved for local task tracking; document contents and protected field values are not needed to report transfer state. Zoom reflow must preserve both the state and the next action.
details.errorCorrection: A bare progress bar without identity or state cannot distinguish two uploads or report completion; a preview or field echo exposes more confidential content than status requires.
details.transfer: If the transfer fails after another file is selected, identify the failed file with safe metadata and keep its Retry action adjacent without revealing either document’s fields.

messages.text: A preview exposes document content and still does not distinguish upload completion or failure.
A bar with no safe file identity or text state cannot tell the worker which transfer completed or failed.
Document fields are not required to report transfer progress and would expose protected values in the status panel.

options.text: Render a third-party document preview beside the progress bar, then remove it when upload completes.
Show a progress bar with no file identity or text status so no document detail can appear in the panel.
Repeat the selected document’s field values in the status panel so the case worker can verify its contents during upload.
Show minimal file identity and transfer state without document contents; keep recovery controls readable at zoom.

prompt: In a legal case portal, the case worker must upload and review a confidential document. Confidential upload progress and completion state must be visible without revealing protected values. Which visual treatment keeps the task status and next action understandable?

constraints: The count must use the active locale plural rules, and the message direction must follow the translated content.
Long translations must wrap without clipping the state label or its adjacent action.

feedback.reason: Plural selection, inline direction, and text expansion each solve a different failure in a translated editor.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Locale plural rules choose the count message form; a direction boundary keeps RTL text from reversing neighboring controls; intrinsic wrapping gives the translated message room without clipping its state label.
details.scenarioApplication: The translator changes locale while editing a counted RTL message. The count grammar and field direction must follow that locale, and the state label and action must remain visible when the translated copy is longer.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Direction metadata applies to the message region, not the whole workspace. Wrapping may increase field height, so neighboring controls must move with the layout rather than overlap or disappear.
details.errorCorrection: Changing workspace direction does not select the right plural form; correct grammar still fails if a fixed English-height field clips the translated state label.
details.transfer: If a locale switch changes the count form from one to a longer plural phrase, retain the numeric argument and state label while allowing that message region to expand in its own direction.

messages.text: A message direction should not reverse unrelated controls in the workspace.
Flexible layout does not correct English-only plural grammar.
Locale plural rules cannot make a clipped translation or state label readable.

options.text: Use locale plural rules, let RTL text wrap, and keep state labels persistent.
Use locale plural rules, but switch the whole workspace to RTL when one message uses RTL text.
Let translated text wrap and keep labels visible, but use English plural forms for every locale.
Use locale plural rules and show status labels, but clip translations at the English field height.

prompt: A translator switches locale while editing a long RTL message with a count. Which treatment preserves locale grammar, text direction, and the full state label as the message expands?

constraints: A failed server confirmation must not appear to complete the application.

feedback.reason: The coordinator needs a durable submitted or failed result and a visible way to correct the missing-document request.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Keep the server outcome as text after the response; reflow the request, result, and correction action together so zoom or high-contrast rendering cannot hide the next step.
details.scenarioApplication: The permitting coordinator requests a missing document and needs to know whether the submission succeeded or failed at 200% zoom and in a high-contrast theme.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A pending indicator describes work in progress only. On failure, preserve the request and a correction action; on success, report the confirmed result without relying on hue.
details.errorCorrection: A fixed banner that covers the missing-document request or its correction action hides the recovery path at the required zoom; keep the result and next action visible together.
details.transfer: If the server rejects the request while the form is enlarged, keep the failure text and the action to correct or retry adjacent in the reflowed form.

messages.text: Button color and disappearance do not state whether the request succeeded.

values.text: Expose a live result message, then retain the same green button after success or rejection.
